entries.name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the athlete began standing upright and the bar finished near the stomach, which the text names as the fault. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 40 degrees so the wide grip and the wide elbows show: hinged over soft knees with the bar hanging beneath the shoulders on a wide grip; the trunk does not rise while the elbows drive out to the sides and the bar is rowed to the upper chest, a hold, and a slower lowering to long arms. Not drawn: the overhand grip.
entries.summary: Hinged with a wide grip and the bar hanging under a braced torso, drive the elbows wide to row the bar to the upper chest, hold, then lower to long arms without rising.

frames.caption: Take a wide overhand grip, soften the knees, and hinge until the bar hangs beneath a braced torso.
Drive the elbows wide and row the bar toward the upper chest.
Hold long enough to feel the rear shoulders finish.
Lower to long arms without rising.
Brace the hinge before the pull. Drive the elbows wide.

entries.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench
entries.reason: Independent draft repair: world-transverse shoulder abduction at fixed15deg elbow flexion; projected45deg oblique camera. World arm lengths12.5/12 are exposed by the production solver for independent inspection. Quiet horizontal trunk and per-body forehead/pad surface contact. No row or front-raise alias.
entries.summary: Raise the arms out to the sides with the forehead supported.

frames.caption: Keep the forehead on the bench and let the dumbbells hang under the shoulders.
Raise the arms out to the sides with one small, fixed elbow bend.
Bring the upper arms level with the floor while the torso stays still.
Hold the lateral raise for one second with the forehead supported.
Lower both arms along the same lateral arc to the hanging start.
